findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud
findings.deal_impact: Spoofable domain increases BEC/wire-fraud and phishing risk affecting customers and deal communications; enforcement is a quick, visible insurability improvement.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none to quarantine then reject, validating all senders and rua monitoring first.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail
findings.deal_impact: Soft-fail SPF weakens spoofing resistance and undermines DMARC enforcement value for a SaaS handling fleet customer communications.

remediation.summary: Audit authorized senders, then change SPF ~all to -all in coordination with DMARC enforcement.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled
findings.deal_impact: Unsigned DNS increases cache-poisoning/redirection risk, though exploitability is lower than email and edge exposures.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at registrar/DNS provider and verify DS publication and chain of trust.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems
findings.deal_impact: Named VPN, legacy CI, staging and legacy portal hosts suggest higher-value attack surface requiring confirmatory diligence on access controls and decommissioning.

remediation.summary: Inventory each risky hostname, restrict or retire legacy/staging systems, and enforce MFA/VPN access for retained services.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size
findings.deal_impact: 47 hostnames for a 201-1000 employee company suggests asset inventory sprawl and potential unmanaged services diluting patch/monitoring coverage.

remediation.summary: Reconcile CT hostnames to a CMDB/asset inventory, assign owners, and remove or monitor orphaned hostnames.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support TLSv1.0: true, TLSv1.1: true, TLSv1.2: true; tls_versions [TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2]

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www may fail customer security reviews and indicates inconsistent hardening across apex and www hosts.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 on www host, standardize TLS 1.2+ configuration across web properties.

findings.title: HSTS not set
findings.deal_impact: Missing HSTS leaves users more exposed to downgrade/strip attacks and signals basic web hardening gap to insurers and enterprise customers.

remediation.summary: Add Strict-Transport-Security header with suitable max-age after confirming HTTPS-only operation on both hosts.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001 ExampleGate SSL-VPN 7.0.11 appliance_exposed product match; KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified.

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure of an internet-facing SSL-VPN appliance listed in CISA KEV; version not verified, so requires urgent confirmation of patch level before close as it could affect insurability.

remediation.summary: Urgently verify ExampleGate version/patch against KEV entry, patch or isolate appliance, and review VPN logs for compromise.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: 2025-08-14 state AG breach notice: unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified. disclosed_within_months: 14; entity_match: exact

findings.deal_impact: A breach 14 months ago with ~3,100 notified raises regulatory, customer notification, and cyber-insurance diligence; require root-cause and remediation evidence pre-close.

remediation.summary: Obtain incident post-mortem, regulator closure status, and evidence of corrective actions; confirm no outstanding notification or litigation obligations.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.1)

evidence.excerpt: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.1 exception: MFA is enforced for all administrative access to production systems.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.2)

evidence.excerpt: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.2 exception: Access for terminated employees is revoked within 1 business day of termination.

evidence.excerpt: For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC7.2 exception: Security alerts generated by the SIEM are reviewed and triaged daily.

evidence.excerpt: 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

remediation.summary: Remediate CC8.1 exception: Production changes are approved by a peer before deployment.

findings.title: SOC 2 report period ended more than 90 days ago; no bridge letter provided
findings.deal_impact: Report period ended 2026-03-31, 213 days before the assessment date; controls may have changed since.

remediation.summary: Obtain a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: infrastructure hosting.

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (infrastructure hosting) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Every admin account is behind MFA. No exceptions. That's been true for years. It's enforced through our conditional access policy.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 sampling found 4 of 25 admin accounts were not enforced for MFA, directly conflicting with the claim of no exceptions.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Offboarding is automated. HR flags the termination and access is revoked same day through our identity provider.

contradictions.explanation: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, contradicting same-day automated revocation.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We have a 24 7 SOC through our MSSP, every alert gets looked at, nothing sits.

contradictions.explanation: For two consecutive weeks, alerts were sent to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed, contradicting the claim that every alert is reviewed.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We're fully locked down there. DMARC is enforced. Nobody can spoof our domain.

contradictions.explanation: DMARC policy is p=none, meaning monitoring only rather than enforcement, so the domain remains spoofable.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: No, nothing material. We've never had a breach.

contradictions.explanation: A 2025-08-14 breach notice reports unauthorized access to a customer support system and approximately 3,100 people notified.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We decommissioned the legacy stuff a while back. Everything external goes through the main app and the VPN.

contradictions.explanation: CT log presence alone doesn't prove a host is live, but certificates for jenkins-old and legacy-portal last seen in 2026, within 12 months, show those systems are still actively maintained, contradicting prior decommissioning.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Annual third party test. The last one came back clean. No highs.

contradictions.explanation: The SOC 2 evidence confirms annual independent penetration testing, but reports 2 high-severity findings, contradicting the claim that the last test was clean with no highs.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Daily backups to immutable storage in a second region and we do a restore test every quarter.

contradictions.explanation: Control A1.2-01 was tested with no exceptions: production data is backed up daily to immutable storage and restore tests are performed quarterly.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We can get one. one we haven't needed it so far.

contradictions.explanation: No bridge letter was provided for the stale SOC 2 period; E-030 is only an unaudited management plan to obtain one upon request, not positive corroboration that one can be obtained.

deal_recommendations.text: Require verification of the internet-facing VPN appliance patch level and a compromise assessment, with a bring-down of security representations, before signing in Days 0–30 [F-008].
Commission an independent review of the listed VPN exposure and validation of management representations within Days 0–30 [F-008].
Negotiate protection for pre-closing incident losses arising from the disclosed incident, with diligence completed in Days 31–60 [F-009].
Plan on the known disclosed incident being excluded from representations and warranties coverage, and address that gap during Days 31–60 [F-009].

Confirm cyber insurability and expected underwriting requirements for email authentication and administrative access controls before close, aligned to remediation in Days 31–60 [F-001] [F-010] [F-011].

Bind the company to complete the remaining access, monitoring, change, email, asset and assurance remediation as a post-close covenant across Days 31–60 and Days 61–100 [F-010] [F-011] [F-012] [F-013] [F-001] [F-002] [F-004] [F-006] [F-009] [F-014].

Make no price adjustment on cyber remediation alone, as the $142K–$643K total is immaterial relative to the 50M-250M revenue band, with work spanning Days 0–30 through After day 100 [F-001] [F-002] [F-003] [F-004] [F-005] [F-006] [F-007] [F-008] [F-009] [F-010] [F-011] [F-012] [F-013] [F-014] [F-015].

narrative.executive_summary: Bottom line: Escalate: full cyber diligence required before signing. Rated D at 56.8 because of a critical, potentially exploitable exposure, a publicly disclosed incident within 24 months, and multiple management statements contradicted by evidence [F-008] [F-009] [C-005]. Key risks: A critical internet-facing SSL-VPN exposure remains version-unverified; a disclosed breach 14 months ago notified approx. 3,100 individuals; administrative MFA and terminated-user access exceptions weaken access control; and DMARC at p=none leaves the domain spoofable [F-008] [F-009] [F-010] [F-011] [F-001]. Management credibility: Of 9 claims assessed, 7 were contradicted, 1 unsupported, 1 supported. Management credibility is materially weakened because claims on administrative MFA, offboarding, alert review, DMARC enforcement and incident history were contradicted by evidence [C-001] [C-002] [C-003] [C-004] [C-005] [C-006] [C-007]. Next steps: Verify the VPN patch level and compromise status, obtain the incident post-mortem and regulator status, secure a SOC 2 bridge letter, and independently validate access and monitoring controls [F-008] [F-009] [F-014] [F-010] [F-012].
key_questions_for_management: Provide the verified VPN appliance version, patch evidence and VPN log review for compromise [F-008]?
Provide the incident post-mortem, regulator closure status and evidence of corrective actions for the disclosed incident [F-009]?
Reconcile the claim of universal administrative MFA with the sampled accounts not enforced for MFA, and confirm current enforcement [F-010] [C-001]?
Reconcile same-day automated offboarding with terminated users retaining access, and confirm the current revocation process [F-011] [C-002]?
Confirm current security alert routing, daily triage ownership and evidence of review [F-012] [C-003]?
Confirm the plan and sender inventory to move email authentication from monitoring-only to enforcement [F-001] [C-004]?
Provide a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30 and the infrastructure hosting provider assurance report [F-014] [F-015]?
Provide an inventory of VPN, legacy, staging and legacy portal hosts, confirming which are retained, restricted or retired [F-004] [C-006]?

exceptions.description: MFA is enforced for all administrative access to production systems.

exceptions.description: Access for terminated employees is revoked within 1 business day of termination.
exceptions.management_response: Management is evaluating an automated HR-to-IdP de-provisioning integration. Until then, terminations are processed manually by IT upon email notification from HR.

exceptions.description: Security alerts generated by the SIEM are reviewed and triaged daily.
exceptions.management_response: The distribution list was corrected on November 24, 2025. Management has added a weekly check that alert routing is functioning.

exceptions.description: Production changes are approved by a peer before deployment.
exceptions.management_response: Management has updated the emergency change procedure to require post-deployment approval within 48 hours.
